slot.brief: Given a relation involving an unknown quantity, deduce the dimensional formula of the unknown (e.g. from a force or energy equation).

stem: The velocity $v$ of a particle moving along a straight line is given by $v = A t + B x$, where $x$ is displacement and $t$ is time. The dimensional formula of $\dfrac{A}{B}$ is:
working:
$[v] = \text{LT}^{-1}$.

From $At$: $[A][\text{T}] = [\text{LT}^{-1}] \Rightarrow [A] = \text{LT}^{-2}$.

From $Bx$: $[B][\text{L}] = [\text{LT}^{-1}] \Rightarrow [B] = \text{T}^{-1}$.

$\left[\dfrac{A}{B}\right] = \dfrac{\text{LT}^{-2}}{\text{T}^{-1}} = \text{LT}^{-1}$.

Independent check: From [At]=[v], [A]=LT⁻². From [Bx]=[v], [B]=T⁻¹. Thus [A/B]=LT⁻¹.
solution: Since $[v]=\text{L T}^{-1}$, dimensional homogeneity gives $[A]\text{T}=[v]$ and $[B]\text{L}=[v]$. Thus $[A]=\text{L T}^{-2}$ and $[B]=\text{T}^{-1}$, so $$\left[\frac{A}{B}\right]=\text{L T}^{-1}.$$
